Subject: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling & throughput sizing follow-up

Hi Marissa / Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo this morning - super helpful. A quick recap and a few follow-ups from my side so we can qualify next steps: 

1) SDK & Auth: We run our inference calls from ECS tasks using IAM roles; we'd prefer an SDK flow that supports role-based auth or token exchange. Do you have sample code for a server-side integration (Node/Python) using AWS IAM?

2) Routing & Failover: Our primary region is us-west-2. We want traffic routed to a dedicated pool in us-west-2 with automatic fallback to hosted API in another region if capacity is constrained. Can you confirm Redwood supports regional routing policies + fallback?

3) Throughput / Concurrency: Our target is ~50 QPS sustained for chat completions (mostly shorter prompts, avg tokens per request ~120). P50 latency goal is <100ms. Curious what GPU count / concurrency you recommend and any guidance on setting per-instance concurrency limits.

4) Autoscaling / Queues: Traffic is bursty during product launches. We want autoscaling that avoids cold starts and an internal queuing strategy to smooth spikes. What queue depth and headroom would you suggest?

I'm attaching a rough traffic spreadsheet and a simple architecture diagram.

Next steps we'd like: an architecture recommendation + rough sizing and a short technical call with Aditya/Dev to validate.

Thanks,
Alex
Product Lead, Acme AI

Attachment: acme-traffic-spreadsheet.xlsx (xlsx)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Alex - great to meet you this morning. Appreciate the clear requirements, summarized below with next steps.

Quick answers up front:
- SDK/Auth: We support server-side integrations using API keys, and we offer a token-exchange pattern for IAM-based environments. I attached a short sample (redwood-sdk-auth-sample.txt) that shows the token exchange + signed request flow for ECS.
- Routing: Yes - Redwood routing policies can pin to a dedicated capacity pool in us-west-2 and include automatic fallback rules to a hosted pool in another region. We can configure priority-based routing (dedicated -> hosted fallback) and region-aware failover.
- Throughput: For 50 QPS with ~120 tokens/request and p50 <100ms, our preliminary recommendation is a cluster of 4x A10/A100-like GPUs with per-GPU concurrency tuned to 8-12 active streams depending on model size and quantization. We'll validate with Aditya given your model choices.
- Autoscaling / Queues: We recommend a short request queue (per-route) of 200-500 requests to absorb bursts, with autoscaling headroom set to maintain 20-30% spare capacity to avoid drops during spikes. We also suggest prefix caching for common prompts and workload-aware batching to improve utilization.

Next steps (action items):
1) Aditya to produce a short architecture/size doc and a sample concurrency/throughput calc (deliverable: redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx) - target EOD 7/21.
2) Schedule a 30-min technical review with your infra/engineering (Aditya + Dev) - proposed slots: 7/22 9am or 10am PT.
3) We'll provide an example routing policy and a checklist for integration (SDK setup, auth, telemetry hooks).

I've CC'd Aditya for the sizing calc. If that looks good, Alex, please confirm the 7/22 9am PT slot.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-sdk-auth-sample.txt (txt)

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-21T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling & throughput sizing follow-up

Alex / team - attaching the sizing workbook and high-level notes. Highlights below; details in redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx.

- Model assumptions: Using a 7B quantized model (fp16->8-bit sim), avg generation ~120 tokens. If you opt for a larger model, concurrency and GPU count change linearly.
- Concurrency/streams: We recommend starting with per-GPU concurrency = 10 active streams for predictable latency; this yields ~12.5 QPS per GPU at the token sizes you've listed (subject to model).
- GPU count calc: For 50 sustained QPS -> ~4 GPUs (50 / 12.5 = 4). For burst headroom (x1.5) set autoscaler target to scale up to 6 GPUs.
- Queueing: Use an in-cluster request queue with soft limit = 300 requests and hard reject at 800 to avoid unbounded memory growth. Backpressure policy: prioritize low-latency routes and drop low-priority batchable requests under contention.
- Cold starts: Keep a minimum replica count to maintain warm kernels (min_replicas = 2) and enable fast-warm profiling (we can pre-warm kernels during deploys).
- Routing policy snippet: dedicated-us-west-2 primary, hosted-us-east-1 fallback with failover after 2s of queued latency >200ms. We'll share the exact JSON policy in the console export.

I've attached redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx with the per-GPU throughput table, example Kubernetes/instance mapping, and suggested autoscaler settings. Also included a sample routing policy and a minimal ECS token exchange example.

Let me know if you want me to join the 7/22 call - happy to walk through the workbook.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx (xlsx)
